mainAnim.title: Turn a GIF into a main-screen animation
mainAnim.lead: Pick a character, upload a GIF or a single image, and the browser converts it frame by frame into frame_000.bin / frame_001.bin …, bundled with the use_slide_frames marker. The device loops it at a fixed 24 FPS. The preview is played back from the generated bytes, so it is exactly what the device will show.
mainAnim.dropHint: Drop a GIF or image here, or click to choose a file
mainAnim.sourceTiming: The source runs for {{source}}s, but the device always plays at {{fps}} FPS, so it will last {{device}}s.

budget.ok: All {{frames}} frames fit in device memory, so playback will be smoothest.
budget.streaming: More frames than the in-memory cache holds (about {{frames}}), so the device streams them from the SD card instead — a slow card can drop frames.
budget.tooManyFrames: Above the firmware limit of {{max}} frames; the device silently discards the extra ones. Please export fewer frames.
budget.frameTooLarge: A single frame ({{size}}) exceeds what the firmware can read; the device will not load it.

mainAnim.checkFail: Format self-check failed: {{count}} of {{total}} frames did not round-trip. Do not use this export.
mainAnim.markerNote: The archive includes the {{marker}} marker file — copy it along with the frames. Without it the device keeps playing an existing main.eaf and ignores the frame sequence.

faq.title: If something goes wrong, start here.
faq.lead: The most common situations, in order. Most of them you can fix yourself.

flashFail.q: Flashing fails, or stalls partway through
flashFail.step1: Use Chrome or Edge — Safari and Firefox do not support WebSerial and cannot flash the device.
flashFail.step2: Check that the address starts with https://. WebSerial only works over HTTPS; both of our sites already serve HTTPS.
flashFail.step3: Swap in a USB cable you know carries data. Plenty of cables charge only and cannot communicate.
flashFail.step4: Close anything else holding the serial port (serial monitors, Arduino IDE, PlatformIO), then try again.

deviceNotDetected.q: "Connect" does nothing, or no port shows up
deviceNotDetected.step1: Unplug the device, plug it back in, reload the page, then click connect again.
deviceNotDetected.step2: Try a different USB port, ideally straight into the computer rather than through a hub or monitor passthrough.
deviceNotDetected.step3: On Windows, if the device shows as unrecognised, install the CP210x or CH34x USB-to-serial driver first.
deviceNotDetected.step4: Confirm your board is the Waveshare 1.85B (ESP32-S3) — the current firmware supports only this model.

soulpodImport.q: I copied the SoulPod over, but the character does not appear
soulpodImport.step1: Make sure the zip is extracted — the device cannot read an archive directly.
soulpodImport.step2: Check there is no extra nesting level: you should have the character folder itself, not character/character/.
soulpodImport.step3: Place it at /sdcard/personas/<character>/ on the SD card, containing profile.json, config.json, memories and prompt.
soulpodImport.step4: Reinsert the SD card and restart the device — new characters load only after a reboot.

bootAnimation.q: I replaced the boot animation, but nothing changed on startup
bootAnimation.step1: Match the path and filename exactly: /sdcard/system/boot/boot.eaf. The filename cannot be changed.
bootAnimation.step2: Use the original .eaf downloaded from the Assets section on this page — do not transcode or re-save it.
bootAnimation.step3: Restart the device after overwriting; the new animation only takes effect after a reboot.
